checks.claim: A spill bucket around the fill pipe catches fuel spilled during a delivery.
checks.why: Environmental agencies describe it as a liquid-tight container round the fill pipe that catches drips when the delivery hose is disconnected.

sources.title: Release Prevention for Underground Storage Tanks (Environmental Protection Agency)

checks.claim: An overfill valve in the fill pipe shuts off the flow when the tank is nearly full.
checks.why: Overfill prevention valves close the fill pipe when the tank reaches about 95 percent.

sources.title: Overfill protection automatic shutoff device (Minnesota Pollution Control Agency)

checks.claim: Double-walled tanks have a gap between the walls that is monitored for leaks.
checks.why: Interstitial monitoring watches the space between the walls with sensors that alarm when liquid appears.

sources.title: Secondary Containment with Interstitial Monitoring (North Dakota DEQ)

checks.claim: Underground fuel tanks have vent pipes that release vapors above the ground.
checks.why: Fire codes require tank vent pipes to end outside, at least 12 feet above the ground, so vapors disperse.

sources.title: Hazardous Materials: Normal Vents (Alaska Fire Marshal)
California Code of Regulations Title 8 Section 5598
